content:
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten had to stop himself on Tuesday from declaring Rep.-elect Marty Jackley (R-S.D.) “the one GOP” House candidate who did better in his district in the midterms than President Donald Trump did in 2024 — as the results changed live on the air.

Enten joined “OutFront” to discuss midterm results that were still continuing to roll in, when host Erin Burnett asked him to tell people something “we don’t know” yet, and began stating Jackley had outperformed Trump in his race against Democratic challenger Nikki Gronli.

“Alright, I’ll tell you this,” said Enten. “Where are Republicans doing well? Well, how about the one GOP — well, there we go, right here. This was actually going — this is, this is live television, folks! This is where I thought we had a rep who is outperforming Donald Trump.”

He continued Tuesday, “But now it’s gone gray. It’s gone gray!”

Enten had been pointing to a graphic comparing the counted votes for Jackley and Gronli in their race for South Dakota’s 1st District, with text reading, “House GOP Outperforming Trump 2024” and Jackley appearing to have beaten Gronli by approximately 85,000 votes.

The map for that district wasn’t red when Enten clicked on it, however — but completely gray.

“So, in fact, I’ll tell you something you ‘don’t know,’ Erin Burnett,” joked Enten. “At this point, there is not a single district that is represented by a Republican in which they are actually outperforming Donald Trump’s performance from two years ago. That is what we are seeing.”

He noted, “We thought it was this one and it literally changed as I was on live television.”

Jackley celebrated his victory last Tuesday after The Associated Press called the race for him around 10 p.m. CT. The midterm elections in general, however, have been a landslide for the Democratic Party.

Republicans not only lost majority control over the House and Senate last week, but also opened a path to potential congressional investigations by Democrats into the apparent corruption and abuses of power by top Trump administration officials and allies.
